subject: Dedicated capacity options and ramp plan for Northshore model inference
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@northshore.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Northshore Solutions <solutions@northshore.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Initial ask: Dedicated capacity for real-time model inference

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking a look. We ran a short pilot with a 70B encoder-decoder model for latency-sensitive inference and want to move to a dedicated reservation to guarantee throughput and predictable cost. Attach is a 7-day baseline sample (token QPS, 95th latency, 90th latency, peak concurrent requests). High level:
- Typical business hours: 09:00–18:00 ET; baseline 45 qps token-level (single-shard requests), peaks ~130 qps for short bursts.
- Target P95 latency <= 220ms at steady state.
- Forecast: ~40% growth in Q3, planning conversion event in Sep.

Can you propose 2–3 reservation options that map to cluster size, min GPU guarantee, and a 3-month ramp schedule? Also include cost delta vs hosted and any fallback behavior if we exceed committed capacity.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Northshore AI
elena.park@northshore.ai

Attachment: Northshore_request_baseline_usage.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@northshore.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: Dedicated capacity for real-time model inference

Hi Elena — appreciate the baseline file. High-level thoughts below; we attached an initial options workbook (Northshore_Dedicated_Options_v1.xlsx).

Quick clarifying Qs before finalizing pricing:
- Are requests uniformly tokenized (single-request per inference) or do you have multi-segment chains that reuse KV-cache frequently?
- Do you want strict hard-limits on burst or automatic spill-to-hosted at excess?

We sketched three options to match your growth profile: conservative (smaller cluster + burst to hosted), baseline (multi-pool with 1.5x headroom) and aggressive (oversubscribe w/ buffer). Each option lists: cluster size (nodes), min GPUs reserved, warm-up schedule (weeks 1–12), expected P95 at baseline, and month-to-month committed spend. Also included a canary rollout plan (region mirroring + failover).

I'll leave technical sizing details to Marissa and Aditya — they can validate the warm-up cadence and minimum live GPUs for KV-caching efficiency.

Next step: Marissa and Aditya — can you review the attached workbook and sign off on the suggested node counts and warm-up windows? I want to get a revised version to Elena by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Northshore_Dedicated_Options_v1.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: Dedicated capacity for real-time model inference (internal)

Karthik / Aditya — I reviewed the workbook. Quick internal notes (technical):

- Baseline assumptions look reasonable if the model has steady KV reuse. If requests are mostly cold (no cache reuse), P95 will increase and we'll need ~20% more GPU headroom.
- Conservative option: 8 A100-80GB equiv GPUs (2 nodes x 4 GPUs) reserved min, burst to hosted with token-level throttling. Warm-up: weeks 1–4 keep 60% of baseline active, weeks 5–12 move to 90% capacity.
- Baseline option: 12 A100-80GB equiv GPUs (3 nodes x 4 GPUs), pinned min 10 GPUs (to keep KV working across pool), warm-up 4–8 weeks ramp. This gives ~1.25x headroom at steady state.
- Aggressive option: 20 GPUs (5 nodes x 4 GPUs), pinned min 16 GPUs, 2-week canary then full roll by week 6. Good for marketing peaks or conversion events.

Operational notes: autoscaling policy should allow short 10–15 minute bursts via borrowing from regional hosted pool with pre-negotiated failover rates. We should include a simple SLA exception clause for overload days (credits or priority queueing).

Aditya — can infra confirm feasibility of pinned-min numbers and if we can offer seamless spillover (no model warmup penalty) for bursts? Also want an estimate on cross-tenant KV cache rehydration time if we fall back to hosted.

-Marissa
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 13:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: Dedicated capacity for real-time model inference (infra feasibility)

Marissa / Karthik — quick infra sanity:

- Pinned-min numbers are feasible with our Dedicated model. For the baseline option (12 GPUs, pinned 10) we can guarantee KV cache residency with negligible additional warmup for hot prefixes. The 10 GPU pin preserves KV locality across requests for the most frequent prefixes.
- Spillover to hosted: feasible but there will be a cache cold penalty (~120–300ms on first requests) while prefixes rehydrate. We can mitigate with proactive prewarming if Northshore provides a small set of high-priority prefixes.
- Autoscale policy: we can allow short bursts up to 2x for 10–15 minutes but after sustained 30 minutes we need to either expand the pool (delay 24–48 hrs) or queue/shape traffic.

Operational ask: include a list of top 200 prefixes or an API to push prewarm sets; that buys ~90% of the cold-penalty cases.

- Aditya
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
From: Elena Park <elena.park@northshore.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Northshore Legal <legal@northshore.ai>, Northshore Solutions <solutions@northshore.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and ramp plan for Northshore model inference

Karthik — thanks, this is exactly what we needed. Northshore is inclined to proceed with the baseline option (12 GPUs / pinned-min 10) with the 8-week ramp to full steady state and prewarm API integration. A couple of asks before procurement:

1) Can you send a concise MOU with the committed monthly spend, minimum term (we prefer 3 months with an auto-extension), and the overflow policy (pricing for hosted spill & credit terms on sustained overload)?
2) Please include a short SLA appendix covering availability targets for the dedicated pool and our right to short-term priority queueing during conversion events.
3) We need a DocuSign route for the MOU and an estimator so our procurement team can provision budget.

If you can get a draft MOU and the HubSpot quote link by Monday Ill loop Legal. Were planning to start the ramp second week of June.

Thanks — Elena

Attachment: Northshore_MOU_Draft_v1.pdf (requested)
